title: S1 radiculopathy: absent Achilles reflex + weak hip extension
vignette: A 43-year-old woman comes to the office due to acute back pain after dragging a heavy box. The pain is located in her lower back and radiates down the right posterior thigh to the foot. The patient describes the pain as "shooting" and grades it 8/10 in intensity. She has no bowel or bladder symptoms. The patient has tried over-the-counter analgesics with limited symptomatic relief. Vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, straight leg raise testing is positive on the right. Right hip extension is weaker when compared to the left. Patellar reflexes are 2+ and bilaterally symmetric, but the right Achilles reflex is absent. Which of the following nerve roots is most likely affected in this patient?

clues.text: radiates down the right posterior thigh to the foot
clues.note: Radicular pain down the POSTERIOR thigh and calf to the foot follows the S1 dermatome (sciatica).

clues.text: straight leg raise testing is positive on the right
clues.note: A positive straight leg raise indicates lumbosacral nerve-root irritation (radiculopathy), commonly from disc herniation.
Weak hip extension reflects gluteus maximus weakness - an S1 myotome finding.

clues.text: the right Achilles reflex is absent
clues.note: An absent ANKLE (Achilles) reflex is the classic sign of S1 radiculopathy; the patellar reflex (L4) is preserved.

whatMatters: Sciatica down the posterior thigh/calf to the foot + positive straight leg raise + weak hip extension (gluteus maximus) + ABSENT ACHILLES reflex (patellar intact) = S1 RADICULOPATHY. Answer E. The S1 root is the most commonly compressed level (with L5), usually from disc herniation.
strategy: Localize by reflex + myotome + dermatome. S1: Achilles reflex, posterior calf/lateral-foot sensation, weakness of hip extension/knee flexion/plantarflexion. L4: patellar reflex, medial-leg sensation, knee extension. L5: no reflex change, dorsal-foot sensation, foot dorsiflexion/toe extension. Absent Achilles + weak hip extension = S1. Reject L2/L3/L4 (anterior thigh, patellar reflex) and L5 (dorsiflexion weakness, no reflex loss).

eliminations.label: L2 - anterior thigh, hip flexion (no reflex change)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: L2 radiculopathy causes anterior-thigh pain and hip-flexion weakness. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't affect the Achilles reflex and the pain isn't posterior-thigh-to-foot. ✅ Correct if: anterior-thigh pain with hip-flexion weakness.

eliminations.label: L3 - anteromedial thigh, knee extension
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: L3 involvement gives anteromedial-thigh pain and some knee-extension weakness. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it spares the Achilles reflex and doesn't radiate to the foot posteriorly. ✅ Correct if: anteromedial-thigh radiculopathy.

eliminations.label: L4 - PATELLAR reflex, medial leg
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: L4 radiculopathy causes medial-leg/foot pain, knee-extension weakness, and a diminished PATELLAR reflex. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient's patellar reflexes are normal and the Achilles reflex is absent, indicating S1, not L4. ✅ Correct if: diminished patellar reflex with medial-leg symptoms.

eliminations.label: L5 - dorsal foot, dorsiflexion (no reflex change)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: L5 radiculopathy causes lateral-leg/dorsal-foot pain and weak foot DORSIFLEXION/toe extension, WITHOUT a reflex change. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: L5 doesn't abolish the Achilles reflex (an S1 finding) and doesn't weaken hip extension. ✅ Correct if: foot-drop/dorsiflexion weakness with no reflex loss.

reasoning: Sciatica down the posterior thigh/calf to the foot with a positive straight leg raise = lumbosacral radiculopathy
Weak hip extension (gluteus maximus) is an S1 myotome sign
An absent Achilles reflex with a preserved patellar reflex localizes to S1
mechanism: Sciatica is radicular low-back pain that radiates down the leg from compression of a lumbosacral nerve root - most often by a herniated intervertebral disc (or foraminal stenosis). Irritation of the exiting root reproduces pain in its DERMATOME (worse with the straight leg raise, which stretches the root) and causes MYOTOME weakness and REFLEX changes at that level. The sciatic nerve derives from L4-S3, and herniations most commonly affect L5 or S1. S1 RADICULOPATHY produces pain/sensory loss down the POSTERIOR thigh and calf to the LATERAL foot, weakness of HIP EXTENSION (gluteus maximus), knee flexion (hamstrings), and foot PLANTARFLEXION (gastrocnemius), and - characteristically - an ABSENT ACHILLES (ankle) reflex, with a preserved patellar reflex. This patient's posterior-thigh-to-foot sciatica, positive straight leg raise, weak hip extension, and absent Achilles reflex all localize to S1. By contrast, L4 involves the patellar reflex and medial leg, and L5 causes dorsiflexion weakness without a reflex change.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro/MSK > lumbosacral radiculopathy: L4 (patellar reflex, knee extension, medial leg), L5 (dorsiflexion, dorsal foot, no reflex), S1 (Achilles reflex, plantarflexion/hip extension, posterior calf/lateral foot).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Absent Achilles reflex + weak hip extension + posterior-thigh-to-foot pain = S1 root.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on radiculopathy, dermatome/myotome, straight leg raise, Achilles vs patellar reflex, or sciatica? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: L2/L3 = anterior thigh; L4 = patellar reflex/medial leg; L5 = dorsiflexion/dorsal foot (no reflex loss) - none abolishes the Achilles reflex.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: S1 radiculopathy -> absent Achilles reflex, weak plantarflexion/hip extension, posterior calf/lateral foot; L5/S1 most common.

keywords.front: Absent Achilles reflex + weak plantarflexion/hip extension

keywords.back: Diminished patellar reflex, weak knee extension, medial leg
Weak foot dorsiflexion/toe extension, dorsal foot, NO reflex change
Posterior thigh/calf to the lateral foot/sole

firstAid.detail: Neuro: absent Achilles reflex, weak hip extension/plantarflexion, posterior-leg pain.
MSK > disc herniation/foraminal stenosis; positive straight leg raise.

memoryHook: S1 = the ankle root: lose the Achilles reflex and the push-off (plantarflexion/hip extension), with pain shooting down the back of the leg to the little-toe side.
